definitions.explanation: A very young child, typically under one year old.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}が{泣|な}いている。
{赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}がぐっすり{眠|ねむ}っている。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{先月|せんげつ}{赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}を{産|う}んで、{今|いま}は{毎日|まいにち}{世話|せわ}をしている。
examples.english: She gave birth to a baby last month and is now taking care of it every day.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{家|いえ}の{赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}が{毎晩|まいばん}{泣|な}くので、{最近|さいきん}あまり{眠|ねむ}れていない。
examples.english: The baby next door cries every night, so I haven't been sleeping well lately.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}が{生|う}まれたばかりの{頃|ころ}は{夜中|よなか}に{何度|なんど}も{起|お}きなければならなくて、{毎日|まいにち}{大変|たいへん}だった。
examples.english: When the baby was first born, I had to get up many times in the middle of the night, and every day was exhausting.

notes:
{赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう} refers specifically to a baby or infant, typically under one year old.

ETYMOLOGY:
From {赤|あか} (red) + {坊|ぼう} (boy/child), referring to the reddish skin color of newborns.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}: baby, infant (neutral)
- {赤|あか}ちゃん: baby (affectionate, more common in speech)
- {乳児|にゅうじ}: infant (formal/medical)
- {幼児|ようじ}: toddler, young child (1-6 years)
- {新生児|しんせいじ}: newborn (medical term)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}が{泣|な}く: baby cries
- {赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}を{抱|だ}く: to hold a baby
- {赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}の{世話|せわ}: baby care
- {赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう}を{寝|ね}かせる: to put a baby to sleep

NOTE:
{赤|あか}ちゃん is more commonly used in everyday conversation, while {赤|あか}ん{坊|ぼう} sounds slightly more formal or literary.
